annotationRationale: Complex quadratic solutions determine the five plane points. Reflection symmetry reduces the ellipse to an axis-aligned equation, elimination determines its parameters, and the semiaxis-focus relation gives its eccentricity.
sourceMethod: Follows the official root calculation, symmetry argument, translated standard ellipse equation, and parameter elimination. Clarifies why uniqueness forces reflection symmetry and displays the algebra leading to h = -9/10.

review.mathCheck: The roots give \((1,0),(-1,\pm\sqrt3),(-2,\pm\sqrt2)\). Uniqueness makes reflection symmetry valid. Substitution yields \(3a^2=-4hb^2\) and \(2a^2=(-6h-3)b^2\), hence \(h=-9/10\), \(a^2=361/100\), and \(b^2=361/120\). Thus \(e^2=1-b^2/a^2=1/6\), giving 7, choice A.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA Q21 on page 13. It uses the same roots, symmetry, ellipse fitting and semiaxis relation, while explicitly justifying symmetry through uniqueness. The resulting ellipse agrees with the page 14 figure.
review.annotationCheck: Complex solving, plotting, ellipse fitting and eccentricity are appropriately assessed; reflection and elimination are defensible prerequisites. Dividing the fitting equations by b² makes them linear in h and a²/b², supporting the elimination annotation. No material gap.
